description: Planner v2: retrieve-then-compose. Embeds the intent locally (bge-small), retrieves top-K candidate SDKs, injects the foundation/AIM tier + dependency closure, then composes a plan from candidates only. Returns { plan: { summary, recommended_sdks[], custom_work[], clarifying_questions[], vertical_pack, complexity }, meta: { catalog_size, provider, audit_status, retrieval } }.

errorCases.when: The Authorization header is absent. NOTE: this is a Next.js App Router route (apps/tenant-workspace/app/api/build/plan/route.ts), NOT a gateway-mounted Fastify route, so the api-gateway authGate does not apply. It only checks that the header EXISTS — the token is never verified, so an expired/garbage/non-Bearer value still passes.
body.intent is missing, null, or trims to the empty string (whitespace-only counts as empty).
The trimmed intent is longer than 2000 characters — oversized-input guard that keeps the compose prompt bounded.

errorCases.message: no candidate SDKs matched the intent; try describing the app differently
errorCases.when: After retrieve (top-K=20) + foundation injection + dependency expansion, resolveCandidates() returns an empty list — nothing in the catalog scored against the intent.

errorCases.message: failed to load SDK catalog: <underlying error>
errorCases.when: loadCatalogWithMeta() throws while reading sdk-capability.json manifests off disk (unreadable dir, malformed manifest JSON).

errorCases.message: no SDK manifests found at <packagesDir> (tried PROJEXCLOUD_PACKAGES_DIR env, cwd/packages, cwd/../../packages). cwd=<cwd>
errorCases.when: The catalog loads but is empty — the packages directory could not be resolved from PROJEXCLOUD_PACKAGES_DIR, cwd/packages, or cwd/../../packages. Typical in a container where the portal image does not ship packages/.
generateBuildPlan() throws for any reason other than a missing provider/key — upstream LLM HTTP error, timeout, or an unparseable plan response.

errorCases.message: No LLM provider configured / <PROVIDER>_API_KEY is not set
errorCases.when: generateBuildPlan() throws with a message containing 'No LLM provider' or 'API_KEY is not set' — the planner LLM is unconfigured. Deliberately distinguished from 502 so callers can tell config gaps from upstream failures.
await req.json() throws on a malformed or non-JSON body — this is not caught by the route, so the Next.js runtime returns a bare 500.

testCases.name: Compose a plan for a financial accounting app

payload.intent: A financial accounting system with invoices, AR/AP and monthly close

skipReason: DEACTIVATED (MUST-60): POST /api/build/plan DOES NOT EXIST in this repository. It is not registered by the api-gateway, it is not served by the standalone registry-mcp (which mounts only /mcp/v1/call), and no handler defines it anywhere - the ONLY occurrence of the string '/api/build/' in any source file is a comment in services/registry-mcp/src/app.ts:79 describing the cloud-builder as a CONSUMER of /mcp/v1/call. There is no /plan route, no build SDK package and no matching app.register line. So this definition was authored against an endpoint that was never built here and can only ever return 404 from Fastify's not-found handler - publishing it would put a permanently-unreachable row in the catalog. It had been sitting as 'manual' with NO recorded reason, which is what hid that. Re-activate with testability 'auto' if and when the planner actually ships in this repo; until then the behaviour lives in the cloud-builder service, not here. This is a ROUTE-DOES-NOT-EXIST case, not the missing-payload or uncaptured-path-param case MUST-49 forbids marking manual.
